podcast.title: Session Musician Career Start (1957) and Instrument Switch
podcast.body: Carol K began her career as a studio musician in 1957. She initially played guitar but made a significant switch to bass in 1963, a time when women rarely played the instrument professionally. Despite societal norms, her dedication to securing gigs led her to master the bass, pioneering the role for women. "She started working in studios in 1957, switching from guitar to bass in 1963."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive Collaborations
podcast.body: Beyond her work with The Wrecking Crew, Carol K collaborated with an almost endless list of artists, including Glenn Campbell, Neil Young, Frank Zappa, Ray Charles, Tina Turner, and later with Frank Black of the Pixies on his 2006 record *Fast Man Raider*. "Glenn Campbell, Neil Young, Frank Zappa, Ray Charles, Tina Turner. The list is nearly endless."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Extensive Collaborations with Major Artists
podcast.body: Carol K's prolific career saw her collaborate with an almost endless list of legendary artists across various genres. Her basslines can be heard on tracks by Glenn Campbell, Neil Young, Frank Zappa, Ray Charles, and Tina Turner. "Glenn Campbell, Neil Young, Frank Zappa, Ray Charles, Tina Turner. The list is nearly endless."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: In-Demand Session Musician
podcast.body: Her studio career began in 1957 as a guitarist, and she transitioned to bass in 1963. At a time when no women typically played bass, she embraced the instrument for available gigs, quickly becoming a key member of The Wrecking Crew, an elite group of studio musicians known for their versatility and high demand. "She started working in studios in 1957, switching from guitar to bass in 1963. And listen, no woman played bass in 1963. It just wasn't a ladies instrument."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Integral Member of The Wrecking Crew
podcast.body: Within a few years of switching to bass, Carol K became a key member of The Wrecking Crew, an elite group of in-demand studio musicians in Los Angeles. These top-notch players were known for their ability to perform in any musical style at any time, and were called upon when only the highest caliber of musicianship would suffice. "Within a few years, she was part of a group of studio musicians known as The Rucking Crew, some really top-notch players who were called in when only the best would do."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Later Career Work with Frank Black and Matthew Sweet
podcast.body: Demonstrating her enduring career, Carol K played on Frank Black of the Pixies' 2006 record "Fast Man Raider." She also collaborated with Matthew Sweet in 1999, appearing on his album "In Reverse" on the song "Faith in You," further solidifying her legacy as an important figure in rock history. "She even played with Frank Black of the Pixies on a 2006 record called Fast Man Raider."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Most Heard Bass Player
podcast.body: Carol K is considered one of the most frequently heard bass players in music history, with a conservative estimate placing her involvement on 10,000 different recordings. "She is one of the most heard bass players in the history of music. A modest guess is that she appears on 10,000 different recordings."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: One of Music History's Most Heard Bass Players
podcast.body: Carol K is recognized as one of the most frequently heard bass players in the history of music, with a conservative estimate placing her on approximately 10,000 different recordings. Her extensive session work has made her an ubiquitous presence across countless popular songs. "She is one of the most heard bass players in the history of music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Famous Studio Bass Player
xref.body: Carol Kaye is recognized as the bass player for The Wrecking Crew, which is widely regarded as the most famous studio outfit of all time. Her work on the Fender Precision Bass helped define the sound of countless hit records. "Carol K, the bass player for the most famous studio outfit of all time, The Racking Crew."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
